prompt: Which pin marks the Mesopotamian city where Hammurabi issued his law code?

prompt: Which pin marks the Ganges River capital from which Ashoka ruled the Mauryan Empire?

prompt: Select the imperial capital guarding the Bosphorus Strait between Europe and Asia.

prompt: Select the Mali Empire trading city near the Niger River bend famous for its manuscripts.

prompt: Select the port controlling the narrow strait between the Indian Ocean and South China Sea.

prompt: Which pin marks the Aztec island capital built on Lake Texcoco in central Mexico?

prompt: Which pin marks the dry-stone walled capital that supplied gold to the Swahili Coast?
explanation: Great Zimbabwe sat on a plateau in southern Africa, exporting gold and ivory toward coastal ports.

trap_notes.b: Timbuktu lay far to the northwest in Mali along the Sahara's edge.

prompt: Which pin marks the Adriatic maritime republic that financed Mediterranean spice fleets?
explanation: Venice sat at the northern tip of the Adriatic Sea, dominating eastern Mediterranean spice trade.

trap_notes.b: Syracuse was an ancient Greek port on the island of Sicily.

trap_notes.b: Cape Town sat at the southern tip of Africa, founded earlier by the Dutch East India Company.

trap_notes.default: Clay tablets and ziggurats belong to Mesopotamia; papyrus and Nile floods belong to Egypt.

explanation: Athens built a naval democracy, whereas Sparta maintained dual kings and lifelong military training.

trap_notes.default: Athens centered on naval power and citizen assembly; Sparta centered on barracks and dual kings.

items.text: State ownership of all heavy industry
